clue.text: Baby eland's content to be left by itself more than once

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, a baby bear or lion

indicators.note: the inside letters of eland are to be left out, so only its first and last letters stay

explanation.surface: A young antelope seems happy to be left on its own again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like 'happy', but it means the contents of eland, LAN, which are left out to give ED.
explanation.definitionFit: A number multiplied by itself twice is raised to the third power, so it is multiplied by itself more than once.

clue.text: Churchgoers go on catering course

indicators.note: to course is to run or flow, so the letters of go on catering run into a new order

explanation.surface: Parishioners carry on running a catering course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' reads as a class, but it is the anagram signal, as a verb for running freely.
explanation.definitionFit: A congregation is the body of people gathered for worship in a church.

clue.text: Two Dutch chaps?

parts.note: 'Dutch' is Cockney slang for a wife (from 'duchess'), so a chap with two Dutches has two wives at once

explanation.surface: A pair of men from the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' seems to mean from Holland; in Cockney slang 'my old Dutch' is my wife, so a man with two of them is married twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Men who have two wives at the same time commit the crime of having two spouses.

clue.text: Departs, following first pairs of dazed terrapins out of the ark

indicators.note: the departs letter comes after the picked letters
the opening two letters of each of the words dazed and terrapins are taken

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: Animals leave the ark two by two, the terrapins looking dazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Departs' looks like the definition, but it supplies D, the timetable abbreviation; 'pairs' fits the ark story while meaning two letters from each word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of the ark is so old-fashioned it seems to date from Noah's time.

clue.text: Relating to drink, I bloat badly — I try avoiding it

indicators.note: the letters of I bloat are put together badly, in a jumbled order
the words I try steer clear of the letters of it, which are taken out

explanation.surface: A drinker complains of bloating and tries to stay off the booze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' scrambles I BLOAT into LIBATO; 'avoiding it' takes I and T out of I TRY, leaving RY.
explanation.definitionFit: A libation is a poured offering of drink, so the adjective describes anything concerning drinks.

clue.text: Travelling through time back to Jonah in poor whale

indicators.note: the travelling, time and Jonah pieces sit inside the word for poor

parts.note: poor land or a poor year is lean, meagre
via means travelling by way of

indicators.note: the back of Jonah is its final letter

explanation.surface: A time traveller goes back to Jonah inside the wretched whale.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a time-travel story; 'back to' means the last letter of Jonah, and 'poor' is a synonym, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Leviathan is a vast sea monster, often taken to be a whale.

clue.text: Source of sugar cane, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for cane is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to cane someone is to beat them

explanation.surface: Sugar cane is said to be the source of sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sugar cane' reads as one thing, but the definition stops at sugar and cane means beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar beet is a root crop from which much of Europe's sugar is refined.

clue.text: It pains me to be wearing present material

indicators.note: the word for present wears the cry of pain, wrapped round it like clothing

parts.note: to table a motion is to present it
ouch is what you say when something pains you

explanation.surface: Someone complains that this present's fabric hurts to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like a noun for cloth; it is the adjective meaning physical, solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Material things are physical and can be felt by hand, unlike abstract ones.

clue.text: Proportion beginning to reach one in a hundred, almost

indicators.note: the beginning of reach is its opening letter
the one letter goes inside the shortened hundred
almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a ton is a hundred, as in a score of a hundred
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Almost one in every hundred manages to reach the start.
explanation.walkthrough: A TON loses its last letter to ATO, and I goes inside it after R.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses one quantity as a proportion of another, like three to one.

clue.text: Domestic problem of depression in film actors' guild

parts.note: a negative is the exposed photographic film from which prints are made
Equity is the trade union for British actors

explanation.surface: A film actors' union suffers its own depression at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity is the British performers' union. 'Domestic' means of the home: in a slump house prices fall below the mortgage owed.
explanation.definitionFit: When a recession drives house prices down, owners can owe more on a mortgage than their home is worth.

clue.text: Honesty is his strangest failing

indicators.note: the letters of his strangest fail to hold their order and collapse into a new one

explanation.surface: A man's honesty turns out to be his oddest weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' reads as a noun, a fault, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Straightness is frankness and integrity, being straight with people.

clue.text: Dear me, I suspect Liberal intended to make things better!

indicators.note: suspect describes the letters of dear me I as dubious, not to be trusted in their order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal in politics

explanation.surface: Someone frets that a Liberal politician meant to improve matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' looks like a verb, but as an adjective it scrambles DEAR ME I into REMEDIA; L follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedial action is corrective, aimed at putting a fault right or improving a weakness.

clue.text: Endless rubbish stuck in which craw?

indicators.note: the shortened rubbish is stuck into the word for which

parts.note: that can stand for which, as in 'the book that I read'

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is removed

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone asks where the rubbish got stuck in their craw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which' is not a question word here but a relative pronoun swapped for its synonym; 'Endless' trims the rubbish word before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: The craw is the crop of a bird, and loosely the gullet or neck of a person.

clue.text: Expressing a slight scepticism about old ways of seeing things?

indicators.note: the answer is lodged about the words expressing a slight scepticism, which carry it within them

explanation.surface: Someone voices mild doubt about outdated ways of viewing the world.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the end of 'Expressing' through 'a slight' into 'scepticism'. 'Ways of seeing things' is literal: lamps.
explanation.definitionFit: Before electric light, homes and streets were lit by gas lamps, an old way to see in the dark.

clue.text: Maiden name used during date by Laura, shortly after break-up

indicators.note: the name letter is used inside the date

parts.note: I AUG is the first of August, a date

indicators.note: the letters of the shortened Laura are broken up and rearranged
shortly means the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A woman's maiden name was used on a date with Laura soon after a split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' looks part of 'maiden name'; it is the definition. LAURA cut short to LAUR is broken up into URAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden voyage or speech is the first one, the opening one in a series.

clue.text: Loves escaping from stores, so foul and mentally draining

indicators.note: the three O letters escape from the words stores and so foul, leaving the rest

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so each love is an O and loves gives several

explanation.surface: Romance flees from foul-smelling shops, leaving them exhausting places.
explanation.walkthrough: One O goes from STORES to give STRES and two from SO FOUL to give SFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that causes strain and worry tires the mind and is emotionally exhausting.

clue.text: Sheepishly talk with senior having invaded Iraqi city

indicators.note: the senior letters have invaded, gone inside, the sheep's word

parts.note: baa is how a sheep talks

explanation.surface: Someone talks timidly with a senior figure after an invasion of an Iraqi city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepishly' means shyly in the surface, but here it is literal: a sheep's bleat, BAA.
explanation.definitionFit: Basra is a major port city in the south of Iraq.

clue.text: Sign of frigidity? Sign of wedding following tip from birds and bees!

indicators.note: the wedding sign comes after the other pieces
the tip of birds is its first letter

parts.note: a hive is the home of bees, standing for them
a wedding ring shows a person is married

explanation.surface: A cheeky tale of a cold spouse and a talk about the birds and the bees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frigidity' hints at sexual coldness, matching the birds and bees; it means feeling cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Trembling with cold is a sign that someone is chilled through.

clue.text: A large group backing US inventor

indicators.note: backing means the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: A large crowd supports an American inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but turns A L SET round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla, Serbian-born American, pioneered alternating current.

clue.text: One abreast of new and original band, we hear

parts.note: ur- is a prefix meaning original, as in Urtext

indicators.note: we hear says the next word is given by its sound

parts.note: a sling is a band of cloth supporting an injured arm

explanation.surface: A musician keeps abreast of a new, original band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abreast' looks like keeping up to date; it is literal: a baby at the breast. 'band' is a sling, said aloud as SELING.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant being breastfed is held at its mother's breast.

clue.text: Husband stepping back in show of respect — or resistance?

indicators.note: the husband letter steps back from its place at the front to a later spot

parts.note: homage is a public show of respect

explanation.surface: A husband walks a pace behind as a show of respect, or as resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at a royal consort walking behind; 'resistance' is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical resistance is measured in ohms, and ohmage is a quantity stated in those units.

clue.text: Umra and hadj regularly supported by one Muslim leader

indicators.note: in a down clue the one letter sits beneath and supports the rest
regularly takes every other letter of the words umra and hadj

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The two Muslim pilgrimages are kept up by a single leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Umra and hadj are the lesser and greater pilgrimages to Mecca; alternate letters give MA and HD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mahdi is the guided one expected by Muslims to restore justice before the end of the world.

clue.text: When in Paris, you prove to be most discerning

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
tu is French for you
to test something is to prove it, as in 'the exception proves the rule'

explanation.surface: A traveller in Paris shows themselves the sharpest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When in Paris' looks like 'when in Rome', but 'When' is AS and 'in Paris' is French.
explanation.definitionFit: The astutest person is the shrewdest, the quickest to see what is really going on.

clue.text: Graceful, narrow ring of bone

indicators.note: a ring encircles the answer, which is held within graceful narrow

explanation.surface: A graceful narrow ring made of bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like the object made of bone; it is the signal that the answer is enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective refers to the ulna, the forearm bone on the little-finger side.

clue.text: Leaves Billericay at last — perhaps Ceylon's warmer?

parts.note: cos is a lettuce, its leaves eaten in salads

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of Billericay

explanation.surface: Someone finally leaves Billericay for Ceylon, perhaps somewhere warmer.
explanation.walkthrough: Billericay is a town in Essex. 'Ceylon' is the island, but here it is a kind of tea, kept warm in its pot by a knitted cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea cosy is a padded cover that keeps a teapot of Ceylon tea hot.

clue.text: Slough's allure is, on reflection, very English (that might win you over)

parts.note: a slough is a bog or fen, so its allure is the charm of a fen

indicators.note: on reflection means the word is is mirrored, read backwards

explanation.surface: On reflection, the appeal of Slough, a town near London, is very English.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a dull town west of London, mocked in Betjeman's poem; here it is a bog, a fen. IS reflects to SI.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm offensive is a campaign of flattery and friendliness designed to win people over.

clue.text: Insult the sovereign, say, when changing sides at the front like a traitor

parts.note: to dis someone is to insult them

indicators.text: when changing sides at the front
indicators.note: the first letter, right, swaps sides to become left

parts.note: the sovereign is an example of a royal

explanation.surface: A turncoat insults the monarch after switching sides.
explanation.walkthrough: R for right at the front of ROYAL changes to L for left, giving LOYAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor is faithless, betraying their country or cause.

clue.text: Sees red Greek's heart in tatters

indicators.note: the Greek's heart goes inside the tatters

parts.note: rags are tattered scraps of cloth

indicators.note: the heart of Greek is its central letter

explanation.surface: Someone sees red because a Greek's heart is in tatters.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of GREEK, E, goes inside RAGS.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is to become furious, the same as flying into a fury.
